title: Final Comparative Evaluation: Custom Edition vs Framework Edition

answers_to_questions.greater_low_level_control: Custom Edition - full ownership of retrieval stack, orchestration loop, retry, tracing, and lifecycle.
answers_to_questions.more_built_in_abstractions: Framework Edition - LlamaIndex retrieval, LangGraph orchestration, Ragas evaluation ecosystem.
answers_to_questions.stronger_measured_retrieval: Framework Edition - MRR 1.0000 vs 0.8333, Recall@5 0.9167 vs 0.7500, NDCG@5 0.9862 vs 0.8167 on the 6-query dataset.
answers_to_questions.answer_quality_superior: No - Custom leads on answer_correctness (0.5984 vs 0.5219) and answer_relevancy (0.2961 vs 0.2394); Framework leads on faithfulness (0.5335 vs 0.4884) and context_precision (0.4524 vs 0.3571). Neither decisively superior.
answers_to_questions.production_performance_superior: No - Custom is faster in the deterministic benchmark (median 1.57ms vs 2.73ms), but 3 repetitions are insufficient for production claims. Results labeled preliminary.
answers_to_questions.more_custom_maintenance: Custom Edition - team owns retrieval stack, orchestration loop, retry, tracing, lifecycle.
answers_to_questions.strongest_reasons_custom: Greater low-level control, no framework lock-in, deterministic performance advantage in benchmark, full ownership of execution semantics.
answers_to_questions.strongest_reasons_framework: Built-in abstractions (LlamaIndex, LangGraph, Ragas), stronger measured retrieval on current dataset, guided extensibility via framework conventions.

acceptance_recommendation: Accepted. The final comparative evaluation accurately reflects all available evidence from F4.2-F4.5. Limitations are explicitly documented. No engine source was modified. No benchmark results were invented.

LangGraph-based graph orchestration executing real agent scenarios
Application-controlled security boundaries (tenant isolation, approval gating, invalid argument rejection)
Deterministic answer-quality metrics computed for all 7 samples
